newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN GOLD SALES ANOMALIES "TECHNICAL" - CSS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN GOLD SALES ANOMALIES "TECHNICAL" - CSS.

text.p: Differences in South African gold sales figures for 1996 are due to technical anomalies reflecting different methods of calculating the statistics, the Central Statsitical Service said on Tuesday.
The Business Day newspaper claimed last week that South African gold sales were underreported by 25 percent last year.
The CSS figure for total gold sales in 1996, based on Minerals Bureau information, was 21.2 billion rand while the Chamber of Mines put them 5.3 billion rand higher at 26.5 billion.

CSS head Mark Orkin said in a letter published in the newspaper on Tuesday that the discrepancy reflected two factors. First, the bureau data referred to sales of gold whereas those from the chamber referred to production.

"A difference arises when comparing the volumes of production and the volumes of sales as reported by the bureau which may be due to short-term stockpiling by mines in the hope of better prices and reporting errors," he said.
Secondly, a difference can arise due to the element of value added by the Rand Refinery.

Orkin said there was a difference between the selling prices of the "pure" gold produced and the "raw" gold received. In this case the CSS would classify the value added as a contribution to GDP of the manufacturing sector, not the mining sector, he said.
